newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka minister flies to Calcutta for water talks.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka minister flies to Calcutta for water talks.

text.p: Bangladesh Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad flew to Calcutta on Tuesday for water sharing talks with the chief minister of the neighbouring Indian state of West Bengal, foreign ministry officials said.

The Indian side was expected to emphasise their requirement for water from the Ganges to flush silt from Calcutta's port, while Dhaka would press home the need for irrigation during the dry season, foreign office sources said.
The Ganges flows into Bangladesh through West Bengal.

The officials said fruitful talks between Azad and West Bengal Chief Minister Jyoti Basu would be a major breakthrough towards reching a permanent agreement on sharing water from the Ganges, called Padma in Bangladesh.
The meeting between the two leaders had been scheduled during the visit of the Indian Foreign Minister I.K. Gujral to Dhaka earlier this month.
Gujral and Azad had agreed that a permanent water-sharing accord should be reached before the next dry season, starting in December, the officials said.
Sharing of the Ganges water has been major irritant in relations between Dhaka and Delhi since India commissioned its Farakka barrage, 18 km (12 miles) from Bangladesh's northern border, in 1974.
Officials claim more than 40 million people in northwestern Bangladesh have faced gradual desertification because of the control of the flow of the Ganges.
The last agreement on sharing the Ganges expired in 1988, and attempts to renew it since then have failed.
